articles.title: Chrome could soon let Gemini auto-fix your bad passwords, and I’m not sure if that’s a good idea
articles.excerpt: Google wants Gemini to fix your reused passwords, but it isn't ready yet.
articles.body: TL;DR Chrome Canary is testing a Gemini-powered “Change it for me” option for weak and reused passwords. The feature is controlled by a hidden “Password change with Glic” flag and isn’t working reliably yet. It builds on a Gemini password feature first spotted in Chrome’s code back in 2024. Keeping track of dozens of online logins and staying safe online gets exhausting fast. But it’s also very frustrating when reused passwords finally come back to bite you , so Google might be building an AI shortcut to clean up that mess. Instead of just warning you about weak credentials, Chrome could soon let Gemini automatically swap them out for you. Spotted by browser tipster Leopeva64 on X , the feature is currently tucked behind a hidden flag in the latest Chrome Canary build on desktop.

articles.title: I Built a Website Auditor That Doesn't Just Tell You What's Wrong, It Fixes It
articles.excerpt: I've used a lot of website audit tools. They all have the same basic workflow: Scan website → generate 47 problems → hand the problems back to you → good luck. And honestly, I got tired of it. So I bu…
articles.body: I've used a lot of website audit tools. They all have the same basic workflow: Scan website → generate 47 problems → hand the problems back to you → good luck. And honestly, I got tired of it. So I built something different. Meet OptiQra . The problem A typical website audit might tell you: Your title is too long 17 images are missing alt text You have broken links Your page isn't accessible enough Your Core Web Vitals aren't great Your content isn't optimized for search Cool. Now what? I'm a developer, so I can go into the code and fix these things. But even then, there's a lot of annoying manual work involved. And for someone who isn't a developer, the report basically becomes a giant TODO list. I wanted the audit tool to actually do something about the problems it found.

articles.title: The Database Marathon — Postscript: Why I Wrote It
articles.excerpt: The Database Marathon started on a bike ride. Funny, given the name. A few weeks ago, out on the bike early on a Saturday morning, I was turning over the week in my head — work included. And it struck…
articles.body: The Database Marathon started on a bike ride. Funny, given the name. A few weeks ago, out on the bike early on a Saturday morning, I was turning over the week in my head — work included. And it struck me that almost nobody sees the whole of it. Pieces show up in dailies, pieces in specifications, but the end-to-end picture is rare — apart from our Team Leader, who I've spent hours discussing the technical details with. That matters more than it sounds. From the outside, months of work can look like a handful of unrelated tweaks — or like someone found a silver bullet. It was neither: it's a long chain of connected decisions, each making the next possible. I thought about writing it up as internal documentation. But a wiki page gets read out of obligation, if at all.

articles.title: Explainable System Design
articles.excerpt: In the context of AI applications, it is important to design an AI system so that its decisions are understandable from the beginning, rather than adding an explanation afterward. This is called inter…
articles.body: In the context of AI applications, it is important to design an AI system so that its decisions are understandable from the beginning, rather than adding an explanation afterward. This is called interpretable-by-design or explainability-by-design. Here, explanation is treated as a core design requirement, not an afterthought. For example: The system uses clear, human-readable rules. The model's structure makes its reasoning easier to follow. It doesn't use complex black-box algorithms. The system records which inputs and steps contributed to an outcome. Instead of simply saying “Denied,” it might say, “Denied because the application did not meet requirement X.” Last but not least, humans can challenge, review, or correct an AI decision.

articles.title: Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave Preview: Potentially Nintendo's Best Strategy Game Yet
articles.excerpt: After playing 10 hours of Fire Emblem Fortune's Weave, it's shaping up to be the best Fire Emblem game in years
articles.body: Ten hours means I've cleared the prologue and five chapters in one of the four story paths, which is approximately one round of the Heroic Games out of I-still-don't-know-how-many. It's a massive game, or it gives every appearance of being one at this point, but thankfully it's not a slow one. Intelligent Systems frontloaded Fortune's Weave with new changes to the combat system and some story developments that, even with the recent Nintendo Direct's protagonist reveal, have been very well-guarded. You learn the biggest changes in the prologue and Fortune's Weave expects you to put them into practice immediately, rather than forcing you through dozens of tutorial-style missions designed to make sure you know how a sword works and how to move characters.

articles.title: Duskfade Review: Kingdom Hearts New Replacement Is the Best Mario Game of the Year
articles.excerpt: Developer Weird Beluga has knocked their debut game out of the park with this action-adventure platformer.
articles.body: Mechanically, Duskfade is the lovechild of Kingdom Hearts and Super Mario Odyssey . Narratively, it's as if Frozen crossed paths with Inside Out . But in terms of structure? It's Jak & Daxter meets Super Mario Sunshine . This is a game with plenty of clear inspirations, and as a result, it doesn't reinvent the platforming wheel, but it is still a delightful 20-hour adventure that will take you through some stunning locales, introduce you to charming characters, and strikes the right balance with its difficulty.

articles.body: One of the best horror films of all time, and an Academy Award winner for "Best Makeup" in 1981, An American Werewolf in London turns 45 this year. To celebrate this big anniversary, Universal has announced the cult classic is getting its very own Steelbook Edition, featuring over three hours of bonus feature content to boot. Preorders for this special edition of An American Werewolf in London are now available at Amazon . That includes the film in 4K UHD, on Blu-ray, and as a digital copy. articles.title: Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave – The Final Preview
articles.excerpt: There are plenty of ways that Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave is building out the features that defined Three Houses. I remain very interested to see how your decisions in the past will have an effect on…
articles.body: Key Preview Takeaways: Fortune's Weave clearly attempts to front-load more of its individual heroes' stories, and we applaud it. The new Blaze Arts moves offer a fun risk/reward system in combat. While you can now hop between story paths, the save-game system might annoy players looking to see everything the new Fire Emblem has to offer. After seven years, Fire Emblem is finally returning to the world introduced in Fire Emblem: Three Houses. There’s a lot of similarities to be found in the structure of Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave, but there are also plenty of ways that developer Intelligent Systems is building out the features that defined Three Houses in some pretty exciting ways.

articles.body: For Phantom Blade Zero, the team at developer S-Game is clearly pulling out all the stops in order to bring its bold and exciting vision for kungfupunk to life. By drafting in action movie megastar and martial arts master Donnie Yen to serve as co-producer on its wuxia-inspired action RPG, the Chinese developer is ensuring that every kick, punch, and scintillating sword-slice is delivered with the utmost authenticity and heart-stopping intensity. In 2025, I was fortunate enough to be invited over to S-Game’s Shanghai studio to get an insight into its groundbreaking approach to kung fu motion capture, and to speak with both creative director Soulframe Liang and Donnie Yen himself.

articles.title: Star Trek: Strange New Worlds Season 4, Episode 4 Recap and Review - (Please Don’t) Play It Again, Sam
articles.excerpt: Star Trek: Strange New Worlds Episode 4 Recap and Review: “A Case of Chiaroscuro” is a high-concept, low-impact installment of Strange New Worlds that looks cool, sure, but also reminds us that a gimm…
articles.body: Spoilers follow for Star Trek: Strange New Worlds Season 4, Episode 4, “A Case of Chiaroscuro.” Alright, here’s the thing about Strange New Worlds. For whatever reason, at some point showrunners Akiva Goldsman and Henry Alonso Myers decided that gimmick episodes were what this show needed. After a brilliant first season of adventure-of-the-week episodes, Season 2 featured occasional segments like “Those Old Scientists,” a crossover with the animated series Lower Decks , and “Subspace Rhapsody,” a musical episode, which lit a fire under the notion of what a modern episode of Star Trek could be. And that was great. But somewhere along the way, the gimmicks became the focus, and frankly, they’ve grown kind of tiresome.

articles.title: How kids feel about AI, in their own words
articles.excerpt: When we set out to talk to kids about artificial intelligence, we thought we knew what we’d hear. We expected some to tell us they were using it to cheat a little, the way Millennials and Gen Xers ope…
articles.body: When we set out to talk to kids about artificial intelligence, we thought we knew what we’d hear. We expected some to tell us they were using it to cheat a little, the way Millennials and Gen Xers opened up CliffsNotes or programmed formulas into their TI-82s, and others to share inspiring ways they were using it. We were also listening for concerns that were less kid-specific, like deepfakes or job destruction. But what we actually heard when we asked kids aged 10 to 18 about AI had tons of nuance.  Many of the same kids who can go on and on about music, rock climbing, or soccer met our questions with words like “bruh” and “meh”—or were so deeply against AI or uninterested in making it part of their lives that they didn’t want to talk about it at all.
